resources.string: The phone as a keys-only music player, with Android switched off.
SETTINGS · used the next time you enter
Android switches off. The screen stays black and the phone keys run a small music player. Longest battery.
Stops while you are in Abyss

• Calls can't reach or leave the phone. Missed calls are not shown.
• Texts usually arrive after you're back.
• Clock alarms don't ring.
• Wi-Fi and mobile data come on only while the radio or a module needs them.
• Music from the microSD card and phone storage.\n• Wired or USB headphones, or Bluetooth headphones paired in Android (switch them on in Abyss: menu › Bluetooth).
Hold the power key for 3 seconds. Android takes about 30 s to come back.
This is v1-lite: while music plays the phone does not deep-sleep yet, so the battery goes down faster than it will later.
No wired or USB headphones are plugged in. Bluetooth headphones can be switched on inside Abyss: menu › Bluetooth.
Abyss is not part of this build.
Abyss is busy (%1$s). Try again in a moment.
Nothing saved yet. In Abyss, press Volume Down + Power briefly to save the song that\'s playing.
Tap to copy. Touch and hold to share or delete.
The captures file could not be read.
Could not change the captures file.
All %1$d saved songs are removed from this phone. This can\'t be undone.
After a key press, before the screen goes black again.
Now playing: your last song is ready where you left it, so one ● plays it, even with the screen off.

For the radio and modules. Mobile data comes on only while something needs it and no known Wi-Fi is there, then the modem goes back to sleep. Uses Android\'s mobile data and roaming switches and SIM 1. Calls and texts still wait until you are back.
Highest quality plays the lossless stream (about 450 MB an hour); MP3 128 uses about 58 MB an hour. Abyss shows the data used on its Battery screen.

In Abyss: waking the screen (● ● or any first press) shows where you were and does nothing else. ▲ + ● shows Now playing, ▲ + ▼ goes back (on Now playing: to the menu), holding ▲ or ▼ keeps moving in lists and changes the station on a radio.
Lets the phone sleep while the screen is off and nothing plays. Not proven on this phone yet: if keys or music misbehave, switch it off.
200 volume steps. Above 140, the safe-listening mark, Abyss asks for a second ▲ press before it goes louder.
Abyss uses the headphones paired here in Android. Bluetooth is off at the start of every Abyss session; switch it on there: menu › Bluetooth.
Bluetooth is off in Android, so the paired list can\'t be shown.
Your own Termux bash scripts, run from all-off: Wi-Fi time, triggers and a receipt for each run. Not in this build: you can\'t add scripts yet.
abyss.* apps from sources you add, with their own screens in Abyss; containers as an experiment. Not in this build.
